newsitem.title: GERMANY: DASA attacked on Lagardere cooperation deal.
newsitem.headline: DASA attacked on Lagardere cooperation deal.

text.p: A cooperation agreement between Germany's Daimler-Benz Aerospace AG (DASA) and France's Lagardere drew criticism on Monday from a key member of the German side of the deal.

Martine Dornier-Tiefenthaler, who through her family's stake in DASA unit Dornier GmbH lays claim to a say in DASA decisions on satellite and guided missiles, told a German newspaper DASA should have contacted her about its intentions to cooperate with Lagardere.

But in the interview, published by the Sueddeutsche Zeitung, Dornier-Tiefenthaler stopped short of saying she would try to block the deal, saying only that DASA was legally obliged to inform her of its plans.
DASA and Lagardere earlier this month signed a strategic cooperation agreement covering missiles, space and defence electronics.

Dornier-Tiefenthaler said she was raising legal points about her family's connection to the deal because the family wanted to prevent any bad management decisions that would lead to smaller dividends.
A DASA spokeman declined to immediately comment on details of Dornier-Tiefenthaler's comments.
This is not the first time that DASA has been the subject of attack from the Dornier family.
Dornier-Tiefenthaler criticised DASA's plans to sell Dornier's aircraft-making business last year, blaming losses at Dornier on wrong-headed management decisions at DASA.
DASA is the aerospace unit of industrial giant Daimler-Benz AG, Germany's largest company.
